artists.biography: Pleasantly inspired by the Beatles' psychedelic period as well as the more heavy riffers of the 1970s, alternative popsters Tripping Daisy came together in Dallas in 1991. Comprising vocalist/guitarist Tim DeLaughter, guitarist Wes Berggren, bassist Mark Pirro and drummer Mitch Marine, the band gigged around the area and began recording soon after. One of the session highlights, "Lost and Found," appeared on a compilation released by local KDGE-FM and received airplay on the station. In 1993, Tripping Daisy did well at the Dallas Observer Music Awards and released their album debut, Bill, on Dragon Street Records. After the quartet signed to Island, the record label re-released Bill plus a five-song live EP, then issued I Am an Elastic Firecracker in 1995. Third album Jesus Hits Like the Atom Bomb followed in 1998. One year later, Berggren's death from an overdose effectively ended the band, with their self-titled 2000 effort appearing posthumously.

perplexity.description:
I Am An Elastic Firecracker," released on June 20, 1995, is the second studio album by Dallas-based rock band Tripping Daisy and their major label debut under Island Records. The album showcases the band's psychedelic alternative rock style, blending melodic hooks with experimental and vibrant arrangements that reflect frontman Tim DeLaughter's distinctive songwriting. It captures a dynamic mix of energetic guitar work and quirky, colorful production, positioning the band within the mid-90s alt-rock landscape.

This album marked a significant step in Tripping Daisy's discography, expanding their reach beyond their initial independent release in 1992. "I Am An Elastic Firecracker" received attention for its catchy yet unconventional sound, helping the band gain a wider audience and critical recognition. While not a massive commercial breakthrough, it remains a notable example of 90s psychedelic-infused rock and contributed to the band's cult following, highlighting their creative evolution and solidifying their place in the Texas rock scene.
